newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources to buy Westinghouse security unit.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources to buy Westinghouse security unit.

text.p: Western Resources Inc. said Monday it has a definitive agreement to buy Westinghouse Electric Corp.'s monitored security services business for $368 million in cash.
The deal is worth about $425 million, including the assumption of certain liabilities, Westinghouse said.

The acquisition will make Western Resources the nation's third-largest monitored security services provider and adds 1,700 employees to its Westar Security subsidiary, which has more than 110,000 accounts and offices in 11 states.
Westinghouse Security Systems, based in Irving, Texas, now ranks fourth, with 300,000 accounts in 44 states.

"This acquisition is consistent with our growth strategy and builds on the natural fit between energy and security services," said John E. Hayes, Jr., Western Resources chairman and chief executive officer.
Western Resources also holds a 27 percent stake in ADT, the nation's largest security services provider.
The companies did not disclose the Westinghouse unit's annual revenues. Western Resources did not say how much it expected the acquisition to add to its annual earnings.
Westinghouse, whose diverse businesses include financial services and broadcasting, said proceeds from the sale will be used to pay down the Pittsburgh-based company's debt.

"The sale of our home security business is consistent with our strategy to focus on our core media and industrial businesses as we move forward with the planned spin-off announced last month," said Fredric G. Reynolds, executive vice president and chief financial officer of Westinghouse.
The companies said they expect to close the deal by the end of the year.

Western Resources, based in Topeka, Kan., is a full-service, diversified energy company with assets of almost $6 billion. Its utilities in Kansas and Oklahoma provide natural gas service to about 650,000 customers and electric service to about 600,000 customers.
Westinghouse's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $17.75, while Western Resources was up by the same amount at $31, both on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
